cohort: The study included 638 pregnant women diagnosed with various heart diseases, including valvular disease, congenital heart diseases, arrhythmias, and cardiomyopathies.
finding: The study found valvular disease to be the most prevalent heart disease, heart failure as the main complication, and identified WHO class IV risk classification, NYHA class III/IV, and pulmonary hypertension as predictive variables for maternal complications and deaths, with the postpartum period being critical for maternal deaths.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was indicated in 62.9% of cases.
